If the request is denied, the MSP denies the request of the GO, and the process ends. Alternatively, if the request is accepted, the MSP performs the measurement. The MSP then transmits the readings to the SP. Regardless of whether the GO was informed of a failure or the readings were transmitted to the SP, the process concludes.

Conversely, if there are no other orders, the waiter will debit the guest's account, and then the process concludes.

0.text: The process at ACME AG begins when the Secretariat receives invoices, performs a visual inspection, and forwards the invoice to an Accounting employee. The Accounting employee identifies the charging suppliers, creates a new invoice, checks the items, and notes the cost center and managers on a docket. They then move the docket and a copy of the invoice to the Internal Mail. The Internal Mail sends the docket and invoice copy to the Cost center manager, who receives it and reviews the content for accuracy. A decision is made if it is in order. If not, the Cost center manager rejects the AP and sends the invoice back to accounting, where the Accounting employee will proceed with the clarification with the vendor. Following the clarification, a decision is made based on whether there are questions. If yes, the Accounting employee consults the cost center managers, then sends the copy of the invoice to the cost center managers. If there are no questions after the clarification, the Accounting employee sends a copy of the invoice to the cost center managers. From there, the invoice copy is forwarded to the commercial manager. If the invoice was in order, the Cost center manager notes their code on the docket, returns the copy of the invoice, and a check is performed to see if all items are correct. If all items are correct, the invoice is sent back to accounting, where the Accounting employee proceeds with the clarification with the vendor, and the flow continues as described previously. If all items are not correct, the Cost center manager passes the copy of the invoice to the next cost center manager, and the process repeats from the point of receiving the copy. The Commercial manager, upon receiving the invoice, makes a commercial audit and issues the approval for payment. A check is then made on the amount. If the amount is over 20, the Board checks the invoice. After the Board's check, or if the amount was 20 or less, the Commercial manager moves the invoice copy and the docket to the accounting employee. The Accounting employee then checks if there was a complaint during the commercial audit. If there was, they resolve the complaint. After resolving the complaint, or if there was no complaint, the Accounting employee gives payment instructions, closes the invoice, and the process ends.
